To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the statistics of natural images drive the response of neurons to be Gaussian distributed and scale invariant, that these statistics can maximize sensitivity for natural image discrimination, that normalization can equalizes these statistics across different stimulus types, and that these statistics can be used to build models for more complex visual tasks.

the statistics of how natural stimuli drive model-neuron responses depend on how the receptive field and normalization are modeled, that the response statistics can be made to closely match those elicited by natural images, that the response-drive statistics are scale invariant and nearly maximally sensitive for natural-image discrimination, and that normalization can equalizes important response properties across stimulus types.
